fields.description: Hard cap applied to every result, after permissions.
fields.label: Max Rows Returned

fields.description:
Off: a pipeline naming a column the viewer cannot read has that column dropped. On: it raises. Either way the column is never returned.

There is deliberately no switch here for user permissions themselves. They are injected by the resolver that builds every pipeline, so turning them off is not a setting - it would be a different program.
fields.label: Fail On Unreadable Columns

fields.description: Off: no new table can be copied into the DuckDB warehouse and the daily refresh stops. Tables already imported stay queryable - a switch that silently made data disappear from answers would be worse than no switch.
fields.label: Enable

fields.description: Maximum rows copied per table into the DuckDB warehouse. A `Nakhoda Table.row_limit` overrides this for one table.
fields.label: Row Limit

fields.description: Memory ceiling, in MB, applied to the DuckDB connection while a table imports.
fields.label: Memory Limit (MB)

fields.description: Off: no model is ever called - verified queries, the query builder and dashboards still run, and `agent.manager.ask()` answers "AI is turned off" instead of guessing.
fields.label: Enable AI

fields.description: Which endpoint `agent/providers.py` calls, and therefore which credential and model fields below are read. The other providers' fields are ignored while they are not selected.

fields.description: API Key: metered, billed per token against api.openai.com or the Base URL below. ChatGPT Subscription: bills against a connected ChatGPT Plus/Pro account instead - traffic is routed to the ChatGPT backend and the API Key is ignored while this is selected. There is no Claude-subscription equivalent: Anthropic has never published a consumer OAuth API for Claude.ai sessions (verified 2026-08 - only Claude Code's own device flow exists, which is scoped to Claude Code, not general API calls), so that option is not offered rather than shipped broken.
